question: The O-ring's compression reaction over the squeeze window — the datum 52 replaced with a generous bound, 73 judged the collar wall against, and 87's (A) needs from below.

source.table: Table 2-3: O-Ring Compression Force, p. 2-10 — under 25.4 mm: middle third (hardness below normal) or upper third (above normal) of the bar
source.read: 2026-10-13, vector coordinates of the PDF page (pdftocairo -svg)
source.temperature: §3.8: force decreases very little with temperature except the hardest compounds (N0674-70: −10 % from 24 to 126 °C)
source.time: Parker gives compression set (deflection not recovered after release), not stress relaxation — no field-life force

assumptions: log-load linear in squeeze between the chart's rows
Table 2-3's thirds taken in the log scale the bar is drawn on
seal length = mean circumference on the groove's inner wall (ring stretched onto it)
the unconfined bars hold at an 80 % gland fill

rim_premise_A.is: with a clamp that seated the rim at assembly the end-of-life normal force is at least f·(R0 + p), whatever the ring retains; the retained share matters only for a bayonet that never seats the rim

missing_data: the compound's own compression-load curve at 15–35 % for CS 1.78 (the band spans compounds)
its stress relaxation over the service life at the capsule's envelope (ISO 3384-type data) — it moves 52's requirement between its two ends
the clamp the bayonet delivers (lug ramp, interference)
the cold-side stiffening of EPDM (raises the reaction)
verdict: The «generous» 100 N is not an upper bound: for a ring under 1" Parker's Table 2-3 puts the 70 Shore A load in the middle or upper third of the Figure 2-4 bar, so the reaction is 96–218 N at the 24.5 % nominal and 160–409 N at the 30 % window top, and the band's top passes 100 N from 17.1 % squeeze. With that top, 52's requirement lies between the clamp at assembly and the 20-year form 52 prints: the lug root at the print floor (SF 2 inside) carries it at the nominal at both ends (1.35× at the worse), at the chain 52 models today (27.3 %) only if the ring loses 2 % of its reaction (0.98× if it never does), and at the window top only if it loses 28 % (0.72× if it never does, 1.11× at assembly); a ring that does not relax makes the lug bind from 27.1 % (26.8–27.5 % over the transcription's ±4 %), and strength, not printability, then sizes the collar wall — up to 0.28 mm at the window top against the 0.2 mm print floor. From below, the ring starts at no less than 58 N at the 19 % floor — 3.5× what 87's (A) needs with a clamp that only seats the rim and 5.5× with a clamp at 52's requirement, whatever the ring retains; only a bayonet that never seats the rim leaves (A) on the ring keeping 18 % of it for 20 years.
